ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-02.body:
$18x=360$, so $x=20$ and the largest angle is $6x=120^\circ$.

**Answer: 120**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-06.body:
After four matches they had $4\times2=8$ goals. After five matches they had $5\times3=15$. So the fifth match had $15-8=7$ goals.

**Answer: 7**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-07.body:
Squares: $1+4+9+16+25=55$. Triangular numbers: $1+3+6+10+15=35$, twice is $70$. The difference is $15$.

**Answer: 15**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-08.body:
The main diagonal from the top left has U, K, ?, T, so its third square (row 3, column 3) is M. Row 1 needs K and T in its last two squares; column 4 already has T at the bottom, so row 1 is U, M, T, K. The other diagonal now contains K (row 1, column 4) and needs U, M, T in rows 2 to 4. Row 2, column 3: column 3 has T and M and row 2 has K, so it is U. The remaining diagonal squares, row 3 column 2 and row 4 column 1, are M and T; column 2 already has M, so row 3, column 2 is T. Row 3 is now ?, T, M, ? with the last square being U or K; column 4 already has K and T, so the question mark is U.

**Answer: U**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-09.body:
The final price is $1.1\times0.8=0.88$ of the original, a discount of $12\%$.

**Answer: 12**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-10.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-10.body:
Let Fred be $f$ now and Alice $a$. Then $a-1=3(f-1)$ and $a+1=2(f+1)$. From the first, $a=3f-2$. Then $3f-2+1=2f+2$, so $f=3$ and $a=7$. Next year Alice is $8$.

**Answer: 8**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-11.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-11.body:
There are $31\times4=124$ pages. Sheet $k$ holds pages $2k-1$, $2k$, $125-2k$ and $126-2k$ (check $k=1$: 1, 2, 123, 124). Page 35 is $2k-1$ with $k=18$: the sheet has $35, 36, 89, 90$, summing to $250$. (Each sheet's four pages sum to $2\times125=250$.)

**Answer: 250**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-12.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-12.body:
Swim: $1.5\div5=0.3$ h $=18$ min. Cycle: $1$ h. Run: $0.5$ h $=30$ min. Total $1$ h $48$ min, plus $48$ s for transitions: $1$ h $48$ min $48$ s.

**Answer: 1 h 48 min 48 s**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-14.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-14.body:
The net rate is $10+13-15=8$ litres per minute. $60\div8=7.5$ minutes $=450$ seconds.

**Answer: 450**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-15.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-15.body:
Each arc is $60^\circ$ of a circle of radius $5$ cm, so its length is $\frac16\times2\pi\times5=\frac{5\pi}3$. Three arcs give $5\pi$ cm.

**Answer: $5\pi$ cm**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-16.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-16.body:
The numbers are $25$ and $20$, with product $500$.

**Answer: 500**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-17.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-17.body:
The sum is $40$. In order $a\le b\le8\le d\le e$, with 8 appearing at least twice. To make $e-a$ largest take $c=d=8$: $a+b+e=24$. With $a=1$ and $b=2$ (we cannot have $b=1$ or the mode would be tied), $e=21$, range $20$. Other positions of the second 8 give a smaller maximum.

**Answer: 20**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-18.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-18.body:
The angles sum to $540^\circ$: $90+9x=540$, so $x=50$. The largest is $4x=200^\circ$.

**Answer: 200**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-19.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-19.body:
Each match eliminates exactly one player and all but one of the 128 players must be eliminated, so there are $127$ matches. (Check: $64+32+16+8+4+2+1=127$.)

**Answer: 127**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-21.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-21.body:
The product telescopes: every numerator after the first cancels with the next denominator, leaving $\frac{\sqrt{36}}{\sqrt1}=6$.

**Answer: 6**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-22.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-22.body:
The vertices are $(1,1)$ (from $y=x$ and $y=1$), $(7,1)$ (from $y=1$ and $x+y=8$) and $(4,4)$ (from $y=x$ and $x+y=8$). The base along $y=1$ is $6$ and the height is $4-1=3$, so the area is $\frac12\times6\times3=9$.

**Answer: 9**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-24.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-24.body:
The main diagonal runs U (top left), K, M and so ends with T. Row 1 then needs K and M in its last two squares; column 3 already has M (row 3), so row 1 is U, T, K, M. In row 2, the last square cannot be K (row 2 has K) or M (column 4 has M), and column 4 also has T at the bottom, so it is U. Column 4 now has M, U, ?, T, so the missing letter, in row 3, is K.

**Answer: K**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-25.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-25.body:
Each semicircle has diameter $10$ cm, so its curved length is $\frac12\pi\times10=5\pi$. Four semicircles give $20\pi$ cm. The straight lines are the four sides of the square, $40$ cm. The total is $20\pi+40$ cm.

**Answer: $(20\pi+40)$ cm**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-26.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-26.body:
There are $4$ colours for the triangle, $3$ remaining for the circle, $2$ for the square and $1$ for the pentagon: $4!=24$.

**Answer: 24**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-27.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-27.body:
Ursula: $24$ km/h $=\frac{20}3$ m/s, so $400\div\frac{20}3=60$ s. Kaleb: $60$ s. Manjula: $25$ s for the first $200$ m, and at half the speed the second $200$ m takes $50$ s, so $75$ s. The fastest leg of the other three is $60$ s, so Taiwo takes $55$ s. Total $60+60+75+55=250$ s.

**Answer: 250**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-28.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-28.body:
One litre of the mixture contains $\frac16$ litre of acid and $\frac56$ litre of water. Adding $4$ litres of water gives acid $\frac16$ and water $\frac56+4=\frac{29}6$. The ratio is $1:29$.

**Answer: 1 : 29**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-29.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-29.body:
Kim's car goes at $30$ mph. They approach each other at $60+30=90$ mph over $30$ miles, so they meet after $\frac13$ hour $=20$ minutes.

**Answer: 20**

ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-30.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2025-regional-relay-30.body:
The minute hand is at $25\times6=150^\circ$. The hour hand is at $8\times30+25\times0.5=252.5^\circ$. The angle is $102.5^\circ$.

**Answer: 102.5**
